text:
Scott Morrow spent a long stretch as a healthy scratch before getting back in on Nov 1, and The Hockey News wrote that he's seizing the opportunity. He's played seven straight, about 13 minutes a night, with one assist, and Forever Blueshirts suggests Matthew Robertson may keep a spot over him once everyone is healthy.

The seven-game sample is small but encouraging. The Rangers take 63% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with Morrow on the ice, more than 10 points better than without him, and 55% of the shot attempts. He's put 13 shots on goal, a lot for his minutes. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that a third of his shots came off the rush last season, double the typical defenseman, and he carried the puck in on 46% of his entries.

The concern from last season was defense: Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level, with opponents creating more against him than against almost any defenseman, in a small sample. The 2021 second-round pick, acquired from Carolina, is 24 and has 45 NHL games. Our talent range has him around 13 points over a full season. If the chance share holds, he's making it hard to sit him.
